clue.text: Face up to unpleasant situation: eat lead?

definitions.meaning: to accept something painful with stoicism, as soldiers once clenched their teeth on a slug during surgery
taken literally, to sink your teeth into a lead slug fired from a gun

explanation.surface: Someone told to face facts, with the grim joke that the alternative is swallowing a bullet.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to endure something unpleasant bravely; literally it describes chomping on a piece of ammunition.

clue.text: Such gains not legit, criminal pocketing pounds

definitions.note: the definition describes the kind of gains meant, so it stands for an adjective: gains of this sort

indicators.note: pocketing means the anagram holds the pound sign inside it, as a pocket holds coins
something criminal is crooked or bent, so the letters of the words before it are twisted into a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A comment that profits which aren't legitimate come from a crook stashing cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges NOTLEGIT into ILGOTTEN, and 'pocketing' puts L inside it. The surface sense of 'not legit' also hints at the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is fixed: profits obtained dishonestly are called by this adjective, describing exactly what kind of gains they are.

clue.text: At great cost, heading off in good time

indicators.note: heading off means the word loses its leading letter, its head being taken away

parts.note: to pay dearly is to pay at great cost

explanation.surface: Setting off promptly, though paying a lot to do so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' looks like departing; it removes the D from DEARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving ahead of schedule or with time to spare is a plain synonym of being prompt or beforehand.

clue.text: Prisoner's name sewn into socks

definitions.note: read as 'Prisoner is', the 's being the verb that links definition and wordplay

indicators.note: sewn into means the label is stitched inside the hosiery, one word placed within the other

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings or socks
a tag is a name or label, as in a name tag

explanation.surface: A captive's name has been stitched into their socks, like a schoolchild's laundry label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prisoner's' is 'Prisoner is', with the definition first.
explanation.definitionFit: A person held captive by kidnappers or an enemy as security for demands is a classic case of a prisoner.

clue.text: Doctor's first in nearby, in this manner?

indicators.note: in means that opening letter is set inside the word for nearby

parts.note: beside means next to or nearby

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word Doctor's is taken

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how a doctor behaves when close at hand, hinting at the phrase for a physician's patient-side demeanour.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is completed by the phrase 'bedside manner', a doctor's way with patients; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's tactful, reassuring way with patients is known as a bedside manner, so this word fills the blank before 'manner'.

clue.text: One who looks for your comments

definitions.text: One who looks for your comments

parts.words: One who looks for your comments
parts.note: sounds like someone seeking feedback, but describes a person who watches mouths to understand speech, often a deaf person

explanation.surface: Someone eager to hear your opinions.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person understands speech by watching the movement of a speaker's mouth, literally looking at what you say.

clue.text: Am leaving US girl

indicators.note: leaving means those two letters depart from the country's name, which is left without them

parts.note: the US is America
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone announcing they are quitting an American girl, or leaving the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Am' looks like the verb 'I am'; it is simply the letters removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a female first name, so it fits the crossword sense of 'girl' as any woman's name.

clue.text: Ver dict?

parts.note: the word for a judgement has been broken into two parts, so it is a ruling cut in half

explanation.definitionFit: A boxing or court ruling on which the judges are not unanimous is so called; here a verdict is visibly divided.

clue.text: Feigning madness, he does succeed to these

indicators.note: feigning is pretending or faking, so the letters of the following words are made into a false arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone pretending to be insane in order to inherit, as in a revenge drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feigning' signals the rearrangement of MADNESS HE DOES.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a job or position one can only get once the holder dies or leaves, so you succeed to them.

clue.text: Star and journalist sharply divided

parts.note: Polaris is the Pole Star
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A celebrity and a reporter fall out bitterly.
explanation.definitionFit: Opinion split into two opposing camps, like opposite poles, is a standard synonym for being split into extremes.

clue.text: 11 is the most popular time for broadcasters

definitions.meaning: eleven has no divisors except one and itself, so it is a number of that kind
the evening peak viewing slot is called by this word followed by 'time'

explanation.definitionFit: Eleven is divisible only by one and itself; and the evening slot with the biggest audiences is the peak, or prime time.

clue.text: Coast of Africa once creamy white

definitions.meaning: the West African country now officially called Côte d'Ivoire was formerly known in English by this name plus 'Coast'
the colour of elephant tusk material, a pale cream

explanation.definitionFit: The country's old English name was the ___ Coast, and the material of elephant tusks gives its name to a pale off-white shade.

clue.text: An infesting ring that may be in girl's hair

definitions.text: that may be in girl's hair

parts.note: an gives the article A
lice are parasites that infest hair, so the infesting creatures are lice
a band is a ring, as a wedding band

explanation.surface: Head lice infesting a girl's hair in a ring around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infesting' looks like a verb but stands for the infesting creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a horseshoe-shaped headband worn to hold the hair back, named after the girl in Tenniel's illustrations.

clue.text: One pitched in river for easing of tension

indicators.note: in means the shelter sits within the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, and another runs through Wales and Chester
a tent is something pitched at a campsite

explanation.surface: A camper pitching a tent by a river to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One pitched' might suggest a thrown ball; it is a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word is used in diplomacy for a relaxation of strained relations between rival states, as in the Cold War thaw.

clue.text: Recent converts see Python broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast can mean scattered widely, like seed, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Newcomers to the cult comedy are told to watch Monty Python on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' reads as a TV transmission but signals rearranging SEEPYTHON.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means new believers or novices, people newly brought into a religion or field.

clue.text: Men aged badly; this is the final stage

indicators.note: badly means the letters are put together poorly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Old men ailing badly as life reaches its close.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess and more widely, the closing phase of a game or process is called this, the last part.

clue.text: Army head pressing to remove leader in a country

indicators.note: the head of the word Army is its first letter
removing the leader takes away the first letter of the word for pressing

parts.note: a pressing matter is urgent
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A general urgently ousting a country's ruler in a coup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' takes A from Army; 'to remove leader' drops U from URGENT, leaving RGENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a nation in South America, an example of a country.

clue.text: Partner of the right type

parts.note: CON, short for Conservative, stands for the political right
a sort is a type or kind

explanation.surface: Looking for a partner who is the right sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' seems to mean correct, but stands for the political right, CON.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse, especially of a reigning monarch, is so called, as with Prince Philip; it means a companion or mate.

clue.text: Usual problem in clay pit

indicators.note: a problem is something to be worked out, so the letters are to be sorted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The common trouble at a clay quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' looks like a noun in the surface but signals rearranging CLAYPIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something normal and characteristic of its kind is a straightforward synonym of being ordinary.

clue.text: Unsound views? I go wild writing about them

indicators.note: about means the manuscript abbreviation goes around the other letters

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
taken as written
to rage is to go wild with fury

explanation.surface: Someone writing an angry piece about mistaken opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unsound' means not real, not inaudible; 'views' are sights, and illusions are false ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical illusions seen in desert heat, such as false water, are sights that are not solid or real.

clue.text: Is East European allowed to dance round this?

parts.note: may means is permitted, as in 'you may go'
a Pole is a person from Poland

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether a Polish visitor may join the dance around a ribbon post.
explanation.walkthrough: The question 'Is East European allowed' reads cryptically as 'May Pole?'.
explanation.definitionFit: On May Day, dancers weave ribbons as they circle a tall decorated post on the village green.

clue.text: Delighted with make-up, but careless

parts.note: slap is slang, especially theatrical, for cosmetics or make-up
delighted means happy

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled with their cosmetics, though sloppy in applying them.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a casual, haphazard, easygoing attitude, someone heedless or slapdash in manner.

clue.text: Trouble as a horse runs over

parts.note: gee-gee, written GG, is childish slang for a horse
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Racing trouble as a horse bolts across the track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' and 'over' look like a horse racing; they are cricket scorecard letters. AGGRO is British slang for aggressive trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: This British slang word, short for aggravation, means hostility or violent bother, such as a fight.

clue.text: Haul up weight a short distance

parts.note: an inch is a small length

explanation.surface: Lifting a heavy load just a little way.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something with a crank-driven drum and rope is the verb's meaning, as when lifting cargo or a boat.

clue.text: Dog, empty, tucks into small piece of cake

indicators.note: tucks into means the emptied word is put inside the word for small

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

indicators.note: empty means the word Dog is emptied of its middle, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A hungry dog wolfing down a small slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks into' suggests the dog eating the cake, but it is the container signal; 'empty' strips the dog down to its shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangular slice cut from a round cake or cheese is called by this name, describing its shape.

clue.text: Has obligation, being hunted to hide head

indicators.note: hiding the head means the first letter is concealed, removed from view

parts.note: sought means searched for or hunted

explanation.surface: A fugitive who, being chased, has a duty to keep their head down.
explanation.definitionFit: The modal verb expresses duty, as in 'you ___ to go', meaning one is bound or should.

clue.text: Docile nun remarkably ecstatic on this

indicators.note: remarkably suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters are made into an unusual new order

explanation.surface: A meek nun who is unexpectedly in raptures.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone blissfully happy is said to be 'on' this imagined height in the sky, an idiom for elation.

clue.text: Shortly take advice with army officer or government representative

indicators.note: shortly means the word is cut short, its last letter dropped

parts.note: to consult is to seek advice
a general is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: A quick consultation with a military officer or an official.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the senior diplomat in charge of a country's consulate in a major foreign city, an official envoy of the state.
